one_line: Prince and last defender of Chauragarh hill-fort, who led the resistance of Garha-Katanga after Rani Durgavati’s death in 1564 CE.

appearance.age_look: Early twenties, athletic and wiry with a disciplined soldier’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, warm medium-brown complexion, straight nose, sharp dark-brown eyes under slightly arched brows, a trimmed jawline beard and mustache, default expression focused and resolute with a hint of sadness.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair grown to shoulder length, pulled back into a low knot at the back of his head, wrapped in a short deep-red cloth band like a simple turban band, with a few loose strands by the temples.
appearance.costume: Over a long-sleeved off-white cotton angarkha-style tunic that wraps left over right and ties at the side, he wears a fitted sleeveless quilted cotton coat (padded armor) in muted forest green with vertical stitching; below, a deep-indigo cotton dhoti tightly wrapped and brought between the legs in a practical warrior’s style, tied with a broad dark-brown leather belt at the waist holding a simple sheath; on his feet, tan leather mojari-style shoes with slightly upturned toes; around his neck a plain black cotton thread with a small, flat metal talisman pendant tucked modestly under the tunic; on his wrists, a single plain copper bangle on the right arm and a narrow cloth wristguard on the left; his ears have small, simple copper hoop earrings; a short, practical brown cotton scarf is slung from his left shoulder across the chest and tucked at the belt, usable as a sash; when in battle pose, a light round hide-and-wood shield with a dark-brown face and four small metal bosses hangs across his back by a strap.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved single-edged talwar sword with a simple steel blade, an unadorned iron hilt with a disc pommel and knuckle-bow, carried at his left hip in a plain dark-brown leather scabbard showing light wear.

ref_desc: Vīr Narayan is a wiry, early-twenties prince with medium-brown skin, shoulder-length black hair in a low knot wrapped with a deep-red band, a trimmed beard, wearing an off-white angarkha under a forest-green quilted sleeveless coat, deep-indigo dhoti, tan mojari shoes, copper earrings and bangle, a brown scarf-sash, a round dark-brown shield on his back, and a plain curved talwar in a dark-brown scabbard, all in forest green, deep indigo, off-white, deep red and dark brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Vīr Narayan of Chauragarh: a wiry, early-twenties prince with an oval face, medium-brown skin, sharp dark-brown eyes, straight nose, and a trimmed jawline beard and mustache, expression calm, focused and resolute. His thick black hair reaches his shoulders, pulled into a low knot at the back of his head, wrapped with a simple deep-red cloth band like a narrow turban band, with a few loose strands framing his temples. He wears a long-sleeved off-white cotton angarkha-style tunic that crosses left over right and ties at the side, and over it a fitted sleeveless quilted cotton coat in muted forest green with visible vertical stitching suggesting padded armor. His lower garment is a deep-indigo cotton dhoti, wrapped snugly and drawn between the legs in a practical warrior’s style, tied firmly at the waist with a broad dark-brown leather belt. The belt supports a plain dark-brown leather scabbard on his left hip holding his signature weapon: a slightly curved single-edged talwar sword with a simple steel blade and unadorned iron hilt with disc pommel and knuckle-bow. On his feet are tan leather mojari-style shoes with slightly upturned toes. Around his neck, show a thin black cotton thread with a small flat metal talisman pendant mostly tucked modestly under the tunic. Add discreet jewellery: small simple copper hoop earrings and a single plain copper bangle on his right wrist. On his left wrist he wears a narrow cloth wristguard. A short practical brown cotton scarf is slung from his left shoulder across his chest and tucked into the belt, functioning as a sash. Across his back, on a strap, hangs a light round hide-and-wood shield with a dark-brown face and four small metal bosses. Use a restrained palette dominated by forest green for the quilted coat, deep indigo for the dhoti, off-white for the tunic, deep red for the hair band, and dark browns for leather and shield, with tan for the shoes; present him in neutral standing poses and turnarounds emphasizing consistent face, hair, clothing details, and his talwar as the clear signature weapon.
